findings.summary: Engine gitleaks config '[extend] useDefault = true' inherits the default GLOBAL path allowlist (node_modules/, lockfiles, image/binary extensions such as *.png); gitleaks-only secret types placed under such paths were never seen while the stage reported PASSED.
Real gitleaks 8.30.1 exits 0 and writes [] when its internal git log fails (stderr 'ERR [git] fatal' / 'error='), producing a false clean.
trivy argv never run against a real binary with a DB; left as a documented gap (no DB download, no install).

investigation: Installed gitleaks 8.30.1 has no command to print its default config and no setting to drop the default global allowlist: [extend] only supports useDefault/path/disabledRules and the extended config's allowlists are always appended. Generating a full config copy was not chosen (would require extracting/shipping the embedded default rules).

Observed with real gitleaks 8.30.1 (scratch repo, runtime-built GitLab token in node_modules/x/c.js, img.png (text) and src.js): 'gitleaks git' with the engine config reported only src.js (exit 1, 1 finding). The same added lines piped to 'gitleaks stdin' with the same config reported all 3 (exit 1, 3 findings; File field empty). stdin mode has no file path, so path allowlists cannot apply.

Observed with real gitleaks 8.30.1: '--log-opts "<missing-sha>..<head>"' prints 'ERR [git] fatal: Invalid revision range ...' and 'ERR error="stderr is not empty"', exits 0 and writes '[]'. A clean run and an empty stdin run print nothing on stderr and write '[]'.

fix.F1: core/workos/security-tools.ts + runner.ts: gitleaks now runs two passes with the same engine config/empty ignore/--ignore-gitleaks-allow/--redact. Pass 1 is the unchanged 'gitleaks git' on the fresh bare clone. Pass 2 (new) builds an added-lines stream from 'git log -p --text --no-textconv --no-ext-diff --no-renames --diff-merges=first-parent --format=commit %H base..head' (empty attributes) via buildAddedLineStream() and feeds it to 'gitleaks stdin' (runGitleaksAddedLines); each finding's StartLine is mapped back to {commit, file, line}. Both passes must succeed; findings are de-duplicated by (ruleId, file, line, commit); per-pass results are recorded in secrets.gitleaks.passes {git, addedLines} (GitleaksPassSummary in types.ts). Evidence kind SECURITY_GITLEAKS_ADDED_LINES added. The stdin input is never written to disk or logs (argv carries no content). No PARTIAL downgrade needed because the gap is closed by a real run, not by assumption.
fix.F2: security-tools.ts execGitleaks: any gitleaks stderr/stdout line matching GITLEAKS_ERROR_LINE (ERR|FTL|PNC|FATAL|ERROR as a level token, 'fatal', 'error=') -> ERROR TOOL_REPORTED_ERROR (fail-closed, even with exit 0 and '[]'); a missing report is now always REPORT_MISSING (previously exit 0 + missing report counted as CLEAN); empty/unparsable -> REPORT_UNREADABLE; exit 0 with findings -> EXIT_0_WITH_FINDINGS. runner.ts: gitRangeProblem() pre-validates the range on the bare clone before gitleaks (rev-parse --verify --quiet <sha>^{commit} for base and head; merge-base --is-ancestor base head) -> RANGE_COMMIT_MISSING / RANGE_BASE_NOT_ANCESTOR / RANGE_CHECK_FAILED -> SECURITY_TOOL_ERROR without running gitleaks. A failure of the patch log for pass 2 -> ADDED_LINES_UNAVAILABLE; a pass-2 error -> ADDED_LINES_<reason>.
fix.N1: Not changed; remains a documented gap.

residualLimits: Value-level entries of the default global allowlist (regexes/stopwords) still apply in both passes; only the PATH part is bypassed by pass 2.

Pass 2 uses --no-renames (a moved file is scanned as fully added) and per-rule path allowlists do not apply to it: more findings are possible (fail-closed), never fewer.
